newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tourists visits to Indonesia up 18 percent.
newsitem.headline: Tourists visits to Indonesia up 18 percent.

text.p: The number of foreign tourists visiting Indonesia in the first 10 months of this year rose 18 percent to 3.43 million over the same period in 1995, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Monday.

Joop Ave, the Minister of Tourism, Post and Telecommunications, said on the holiday island of Bali on Sunday that the tourists were estimated to have spent more than $3.43 billion, up 19.4 percent from the same period last year.

Ave said the figure for the 10 months to October was slightly higher than the 3.42 million the government had predicted. He said between 340,000 and 361,700 foreign visitors were expected to visit the country in November and between 384,300 and 405,900 in December.

The newspaper said the government expected Indonesia to earn at least $6.4 billion in revenue from between 4.78 million and 5.05 million foreign visitors, including tourists, in 1996. This compares with the $5.2 billion it earned from 4.32 million foreign visitors in 1995.
